timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The festivities are in the air and the preparations for it had already started at Sunenna's house.
Her uncle brought the decorative items and her mother started preparing for the food items.
Dad started cleaning the house. Amidst all of this, Sunenna was walking around with a doll in her hand.
She saw her cousin brother Mukul playing and asked,
Where is Auntie Mukul?
Sonenna didi, Ma is stretching in her room.
As soon as she heard this, Sonenna ran to her auntie.
Auntie, Auntie, will you help me?
Yes, Sonenna, I will do it. What is the matter?
Festivals are approaching and everyone is bringing new clothes at home.
I want my doll to be a new and colorful clothes too.
I will need your help and this.
I have stitched many clothes now. There is a lot of clipping left in them.
We can make new clothes for your doll by the leftover clippings.
Take this bag full of clippings. Pick whatever you like from it.
Oh wow, there are many colorful clothes in it.
Yes, Sonenna, it has different types of fabrics such as cotton, silk and synthetic.
You can make a frock or silver camees for your doll from any of them.
All these clothes are so beautiful.
Auntie, how are such beautiful clothes made?
Sonenna, India is famous all over the world for making different kinds of clothes.
The dress of each province of India is different.
And the clothes which are made there are also of different types.
Cotton, silk, velvet, woolen, all kinds of cloth are made in small factories and workshops.
Sonenna, if you look at the clothes carefully, then you will know that every cloth is made up of weaving threads.
Oh yeah, it looks like a thread mat.
Auntie, if the cloth is made up of thread, then where do these threads come from?
To answer this question of Sonenna, her auntie removes thread from her sewing machine
and scratches it into thin parts and shows it to Sonenna.
Sonenna, these thin hair like strands which are coming out of this thread are called fibers.
Threads are made from these fibers and then fabric is produced from them.
This is very interesting, I will tell my friends about this.
But auntie, I have never seen the fibers around.
All these produce a particular place.
Sonenna, the fibers which are used to make different types of clothes are found in different places.
We get fiber from plants and animals.
Examples of fibers that we get from plants are cotton and jute.
Silk and wool are the examples of fibers obtained from animals.
These types of fibers are known as natural fibers.
Earlier clothes made of natural fibers were used.
But from few years, fibers are also being made using chemical materials.
These are called synthetic fibers.
Auntie, what type of clothes is made using such fibers?
They produce fabrics such as nylon, polyester and acrylic.
Sonenna, now look around yourself and find things that have clothes made using natural fibers.
This area of wearing looks like a cotton cloth.
So this is an example of garment made up of natural fibers and this table cloth.
It appears to be fabric made up of synthetic fibers.
Absolutely correct, Sonenna.
This table cloth is made of nylon.
Auntie also made a beautiful frock for Sonenna's doll, which made Sonenna very happy.
Sonenna thanked her aunt and dressed the doll in her new clothes.
Then Sonenna ran to her friends.
Samina, Mohan, Subi, look how beautiful frock my auntie made for my doll.
And sitting with my aunt today, I also learnt a lot about clothes.
Really tell us to Sonenna.
I came to know that the clothes we wear all made up of threads and threads are made of even thinner elements called fibers.
What is fiber?
Remember the day when we were playing catch up and you fell down, your pants got torn from the knee.
At that time, something threads come out of the torn area.
There are fibers, fibers are of two types.
One is natural, which we get from plants and animals.
And the second one is synthetic, which is produced from chemical substances.
Yes, I have also heard about this from my father. He works in a clothing factory.
Oh wow, I don't be asked him how the fabric is made from fibers.
Good idea, let's go.
And then all the children ran towards Mohan's house to learn more about clothes.
